::: {#exm-membership-inference}

#### A threshold from a shadow network

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
shadow_rows = order[1000:1100]
shadow = fit(shadow_rows, width=256, seed=1)
threshold = losses(shadow, shadow_rows).max()
hit_rate = (member_loss <= threshold).float().mean().item()
false_alarm = (outsider_loss <= threshold).float().mean().item()
attack_acc = (hit_rate + 1 - false_alarm) / 2
print(threshold.item(), hit_rate, false_alarm, attack_acc)
# Stop the render if the prose below stops being true.
assert attack_acc > 0.6
```

The attacker of @exr-membership does not know which [loss](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-loss-function) counts as small for the target network.
So the attacker trains a shadow network of the same kind on `r py$n_members` digits of their own,
and takes the largest loss of the shadow network on those digits as a threshold.
The attack guesses that an image was in the target's [training set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-training-set) if the target's loss on it is below the threshold.
This [membership inference attack](#def-membership-inference) flags `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$hit_rate)` of the target's training digits
and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$false_alarm)` of the other digits.
On a set of images half of which were in the training set,
it guesses right `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * py$attack_acc)` of the time,
where a coin would guess right 50% of the time.
@shokri2017membership train many shadow models and a classifier on their outputs,
and @yeom2018privacy guess from the loss alone;
this example joins the two ideas in the simplest way.

:::
